title: GEM: GPU-Accelerated Emulator-Inspired RTL Simulation
problem: CPU-based RTL simulators face scalability bottlenecks; FPGA emulators are expensive and inaccessible; prior GPU acceleration fails due to heterogeneous circuit partitions conflicting with SIMT parallelism.
motivation: High-speed circuit verification is critical for design closure; democratizing RTL simulation with affordable GPU hardware would accelerate design cycles.
method: GEM introduces a virtual Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architecture inspired by FPGA emulator design, optimized for CUDA execution. The circuit logic is mapped to the VLIW architecture via a CAD flow analogous to FPGA place-and-route, mitigating irregular memory access patterns and thread divergence that prevented prior GPU simulators from achieving speedup.
key_novelty: First GPU-accelerated RTL simulator using virtual VLIW architecture to bridge the gap between circuit heterogeneity and GPU's SIMT execution model.
contributions: Novel virtual VLIW architecture enabling efficient GPU-based RTL simulation
Circuit-to-VLIW mapping flow using FPGA CAD-like methodology
Solution to thread divergence and irregular memory access on GPUs
Up to 64x speedup over best CPU simulators
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated RTL simulation via VLIW architecture
